chunks: A man came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and confessed to theft. Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said to him: “Do you recite anything from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic?” He said: “Yes, Sūrat al-Baqarah.” So he said: “I have granted your hand for the sake of Sūrat al-Baqarah.”
Then al-Ashʿath said: “Are you suspending one of the limits of Allah, Exalted is He?” He said: “And what do you know of what this is?”
When the evidence is established, it is not for the Imam to pardon; but when the man confesses against himself, then that belongs to the Imam: if he wills, he pardons, and if he wills, he cuts.

key_terms.السَّرِقَةِ: the act of theft confessed by the man
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam as the lawful authority in judging and applying the ruling
key_terms.حُدُودِ اللَّهِ: the legal limits and punishments set by Allah
key_terms.سُورَةَ الْبَقَرَةِ: Sūrat al-Baqarah, mentioned here by the confessor
key_terms.كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: the Book of Allah, meaning the Qur'an

ai.seo_question: Can the Imam pardon the hadd punishment for theft after a person confesses?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a jurisprudential distinction in the hadd of theft between a case proven by formal evidence and one established by a voluntary confession. Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام teaches that when proof is established the Imam does not pardon, but when a person confesses against himself, the matter is left to the Imam’s discretion.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5106 - A man came to Commander of the Faithful (as) and confessed to theft.
Commander of the Faithful (as) asked him: "Do you recite anything from the Book of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic?"
The man replied: "Yes, Surah Al-Baqarah."
Imam (as) said: "I have pardoned your hand for the sake of Surah Al-Baqarah."

Al-Ashath objected, saying: "Are you suspending one of the punishments prescribed by Allah (swt), the Exalted?"
Commander of the Faithful (as) replied: "And what do you know about this matter?

When evidence is established, the Imam has no authority to pardon, but when a man confesses against himself, then it is up to the Imam - if he wishes, he may pardon, and if he wishes, he may order the cutting."
